title: Golden byte-parity: tag ordering, char-ID order, depth reuse, gradient-fill expansion
description: Tracking task for the DOCUMENTED byte-level gaps between our golden FLA->SWF publish and canonical Flash 8 (surfaced by tools/golden-parity.mjs; all are semantically inert — Ruffle renders identically — so DECOMPRESSED bytes differ but no field is wrong). Gaps: (1) TAG ORDERING: we hoist all character definitions before frame 1; Flash interleaves defs per-frame before first use, and emits DoAction/FrameLabel at frame START not end. (2) CHAR-ID ORDER: we number in library order, Flash in usage order. (3) DEPTH VALUES: Flash reuses depths freed by RemoveObject (d1,d3); we allocate monotonically (d3,d4) — relative z-order identical. (4) GRADIENT FILL EXPANSION: Flash expands one FLA gradient into ~17 DefineShape fillStyles at publish; we emit 1. (5) zlib CWS deflate stream is impl-specific -> compressed bytes never bit-identical; compare decompressed. Achieving true byte-for-byte requires replicating Flash's tag interleaving, ID/depth allocation, and gradient encoding (large, low ROI). Decision: pursue only if a downstream consumer needs exact bytes. Harness: node tools/golden-parity.mjs (semantic parity PASSES; these listed as KNOWN-GAP).
